title: Non-Self-Adjoint Sturm-Liouville Problem for Complex Canonical Jacobi Differential Equation on Imaginary Axis and Associated Finite Orthogonal Sequences of Squared-Value Integrable i-Jacobi Polynomials
content: The paper advances the fresh notion of finitely many complex Jacobi polynomials with absolute values square integrable on the imaginary axis. As a basis for the new approach, we formulate of the non-self-adjoint Sturm-Liouville problem (SLP) for the ‘i-Jacobi reference’ (i-JRef) canonical Sturm-Liouville equation’ (CSLE), which is obtained by expressing the complex canonical Jacobi differential equation (c-CJDE) in terms of the imaginary variable.. It is shown that there exist two finite sequences of the complex quasi-rational eigenfunctions, with the square integrable absolute values. To be more precise, one can consider any SLE, sharing the given canonical form, and then integrate the squared absolute values of the resultant eigenfunctions with the proper positive weight. It was proven that the polynomial components of the constructed (also quasi-rational) eigenfunctions are mutually orthogonal with the almost-everywhere holomorphic (AEH) weight, as a natural extension of Askey’s renowned theorem for the i-Jacobi polynomials with real indexes. By performing the Liouville transformation to the non-Hermitian Schrödinger equation, we demonstrate how the developed formalism lays the rigorous foundation for (more familiar to physicists) studies on bound energy states in the generally non-PT-symmetric ‘Scarf II’ potential.
